form7-64.claim: The News Minute found that 40,006 electors were named for deletion in Form 7 applications in Andhra Pradesh between 29 September and 10 October, the last 12 days of claims and objections, and that 20,959 of them had an Electoral Registration Officer or an Assistant Electoral Registration Officer named as the objector in the Commission's consolidated Form 10 statements. form7-67.claim: The 796 Form 7 applications that name 20 booth level agents appointed by the BJP as objectors in Delhi's Mustafabad constituency are mostly concentrated in 25 of its 294 polling booths, in the neighbourhoods of Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur and Chandu Nagar, The Hindu reported on 10 November. The paper reports that all of them are against Muslim electors and that they are over 76% of the 1,044 deletion applications received in the constituency up to 4 November, from the published data. The applications give absence, a permanent shift or death as the reason, and the paper found at least 87 of the electors named living at their registered addresses. The paper reports, from an analysis of records and interviews with local BJP workers, that the 25 booths appeared to have been selected because they had a sizeable Muslim population and, by the workers' claims, few names left off the draft roll. BJP leaders who spoke to it on condition of anonymity said that after the draft of 31 August party workers compared the number of names placed on the list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors in booths with a majority of Muslim electors and in booths with a majority of Hindu electors, prepared lists of Muslim electors, which the paper says it saw, and then concentrated on the 25 booths, where the agents began filing from the first week of October. The paper says it found copies of these booths' rolls, with the names of Muslim electors marked on them, with BJP workers in the area. It reports that the Commission's booth-wise figures do not bear out the workers' claim. By its count, names left off the draft averaged 274 a booth in Mustafabad and reached 538 at the most, and in most of the 25 booths they were close to the average. Parts 108 and 129, which it counts among the five booths with the fewest names left off the draft, carry 35 and 37 of the agents' applications. No application names a BJP agent in the other three, which BJP workers said were mostly Hindu. Nehru Vihar has the most applications, 496. The paper reports that none of the Form 7s received in Mustafabad came with the undertaking an agent must give.

form7-68.claim: Amit Sanap, the electoral registration officer for Bhiwandi East, told the Hindustan Times that his office had received 540 Form 7 applications seeking deletions in the constituency and had rejected over 450 of them, because the electors the forms said were not living at their addresses were found living there. The paper reports that political parties' booth level agents filed 480 of the 540 and that some applicants could face criminal action for false information. Sanap said some applicants had withdrawn their applications and that action would begin once the formal orders were prepared. The paper reports that Form 7s filed by agents and private complainants have been withdrawn or rejected in large numbers on scrutiny in Mumbai and the constituencies around it, after Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer told registration officers to place the burden of proof on the objector, to summon objectors and verify their claims before acting, and to begin criminal action against false filings. A senior state election official told the paper that objectors are allowed to withdraw, and that withdrawals began once action started and the first FIR was registered in Dharavi three weeks earlier (form7-55). With claims and objections due to close on Friday, 13 November, the Commission had received over 23 lakh forms for additions, deletions and corrections in Maharashtra, more than 95,000 of them Form 7s, the paper reports.

He said anyone with credible information about an incorrect registration has the right to file a Form 7 and that the authorised officer decides whether it is correct.
